http://www.businessghana.com/site/news/b.text: +233(0)303-966-922 info@businessghana.com Contact Us Login Sign Up Home News Business Warsaw Sweet Tech 2026 to showcase the future of confectionery, bakery, ice cream and coffee in ... From September 15–17, 2026 , Ptak Warsaw Expo in Nadarzyn, Poland, will host Warsaw Sweet Tech 2026 – an international trade fair dedicated to the confectionery, bakery, ice cream and coffee sectors. Bringing together manufacturers, technology providers, distributors, business owners and industry professionals, the event offers a unique opportunity to discover the latest innovations, exchange expertise, and establish valuable business partnerships. For three days, Poland will become a meeting point for companies shaping the future of the sweet industry. A Business Platform for the Entire Sweet Industry The confectionery and bakery market continues to evolve in response to changing consumer expectations, technological progress and growing demand for premium-quality products . Companies are investing in automation, efficient production processes, sustainable solutions and innovative product development to remain competitive in a rapidly changing marketplace. Warsaw Sweet Tech has been created to support this transformation by connecting manufacturers, suppliers and decision-makers from across the industry. The exhibition provides a comprehensive overview of modern technologies, ingredients, equipment and services while creating an environment where professionals can exchange ideas, discover new business opportunities and strengthen existing partnerships. Innovation at Every Stage of Production Visitors will have the opportunity to explore a broad range of solutions dedicated to confectionery, bakery and ice cream production. Exhibitors will showcase advanced processing machinery, baking equipment, refrigeration systems, packaging technologies, production lines, ingredients, raw materials, decorations and accessories designed to improve efficiency and product quality. The event is an excellent place to compare technologies, meet suppliers directly and learn about solutions that help businesses optimize production while responding to emerging consumer trends. Coffee Takes Centre Stage An important part of Warsaw Sweet Tech is its strong focus on the coffee sector, reflecting the growing importance of cafés, specialty coffee and premium coffee experiences within the hospitality industry. Visitors will discover solutions for modern coffee businesses, including professional espresso machines, coffee grinders, brewing equipment, café accessories and innovative technologies supporting everyday operations. Suppliers of coffee products and equipment will present solutions tailored to both independent cafés and larger hospitality businesses. As consumer expectations continue to rise, coffee quality has become an essential element of the customer experience. Warsaw Sweet Tech provides an excellent opportunity to explore the latest developments in coffee preparation, equipment and café management while connecting with companies driving innovation in this rapidly expanding market. Knowledge and Inspiration Alongside the exhibition, visitors will have access to the Sweet Tech International Congress , where experts and industry representatives will discuss current trends, technological developments and market opportunities. The conference complements the exhibition by creating a space for professional dialogue and knowledge exchange, helping participants better understand the future direction of the sweet industry. Networking That Creates New Opportunities One of the greatest strengths of Warsaw Sweet Tech is the opportunity to meet industry professionals face-to-face. Business owners, manufacturers, distributors, technology providers and hospitality representatives come together in one location, creating ideal conditions for networking, collaboration and long-term business development. Whether companies are looking for new suppliers , business partners or inspiration for future investments, the exhibition offers countless opportunities to establish valuable professional relationships. Discover the Future of the Sweet Industry in Poland Warsaw Sweet Tech is much more than a trade fair – it is a meeting place for innovation, technology and business. Every edition brings together professionals eager to explore new solutions, exchange knowledge and shape the future of confectionery, bakery, ice cream and coffee businesses. By combining an extensive exhibition with an international conference and outstanding networking opportunities, the event has become one of the most important meeting points for the sweet industry in Central and Eastern Europe. Join us on September 15–17, 2026 , at Ptak Warsaw Expo in Nadarzyn, Poland, and discover the innovations, technologies and business opportunities shaping the future of the confectionery, bakery, ice cream and coffee industries. We look forward to welcoming you to Warsaw Sweet Tech 2026 ! Date & Venue 15–17 September 2026 Ptak Warsaw Expo , Nadarzyn near Warsaw, Poland Opening Hours 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM Getting There Free parking and convenient access from Warsaw by bus lines 703 and 711 . Registration Free admission upon online registration. REGISTER NOW

https://www.dw.com/en/us-tourist-killed-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IyxJ Dramatic images of glowing lava and towers of smoke have drawn large numbers of tourists to Etna Image: Salvatore Allegra/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Italian media report that a US citizen, either 29 or 30 years of age, was struck by lightning Sunday evening while hiking on Mount Etna on the Italian island of Sicily. He died of cardiac arrest while a helicopter rescue team attempted to resuscitate him. The man is thought to have been hiking alone, seemingly in a prohibited area on Etna's eastern slope, which is experiencing extraordinary volcanic activity at the moment. Etna's eruption draws in more tourists Etna, the tallest active volcano in Europe at 3,324 meters (almost 11,000 feet), attracts throngs of tourists, even more so now, as visitors flock to get pictures of dramatic lava fountains and smoke. Etna's activity has disrupted international air travel Image: Etna Walk/AFP Authorities say the man may have ignored closure markings on Sunday to climb up toward a new crater when he got caught in a storm. According to emergency services, the US national was in a state of cardiac arrest when a helicopter rescue crew arrived around 8 p.m. local time (18:00 GMT). He is believed to have been struck by lightning as he wandered the barren heights above the tree line. Rescue workers tried resuscitate the man when they extracted him from the Rocca Capra area of the mountain, some 1,400 meters above sea level. He was pronounced dead on arrival at Cannizzaro Hospital in nearby Catania. An investigation into the incident is ongoing. A train trip to Italy's Mount Etna To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Weather patterns add to risks of volcanic activity Italian authorities have repeatedly warned of the dangers presented by Etna's activity. However, the natural phenomenon remains also a magnet for photo-hungry tourists and thrill seekers. In addition to being an active volcano, Etna is also a very large mountain with potentially hazardous areas and specific weather conditions. Italy's civil protection agency warns volcanic activity and sudden weather changes could create an especially risky combination. The nearby international airport in Catania has suffered numerous disruptions as a result of massive smoke plumes that fill the air with gritty, dry micro-particles that make breathing difficult and act like ice on roads. https://www.wndu.com/2026/09/12/bunks-ac.text: Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google WARSAW, Ind. (WNDU) - Dozens of volunteers with Sleep in Heavenly Peace built about 70 beds for children during a Bunks Across America event. Both the Kosciusko and Fulton county chapters teamed up in the Warsaw Lowe’s parking lot. Kids who received beds now help build them 8-year-old Corie Pierce and 11-year-old Rion Pierce received new beds from Sleep in Heavenly Peace about a month or two ago. “I got on it and I screamed as loud as I could into my bed, I was so excited,” Corie Pierce said. “We had this bunk bed, but they were like spring beds and it kept stabbing us while we slept,” Rion Pierce said. Their mom discovered the local chapter for Sleep in Heavenly Peace. Her application was approved and soon after, Corie and Rion came home one school day to new beds. On Saturday, they helped build beds for other kids. “I really want other kids to feel what I felt,” Corie Pierce said. About the organization National nonprofit Sleep in Heavenly Peace provides free beds to kids ages 3 to 17. “They say 3% of the population represents kids that don’t have beds... we have delivered over 800 since we started our chapter,” said Michael Webb, co-president of the Kosciusko County SHP chapter. Webb went to the Warsaw Lowe’s store manager a few years ago about teaming up for Bunks Across America. They started with about 20 volunteers in their parking lot. This year, there were about 100. Lowe’s not only donated about 400 pieces of wood this year, they bought breakfast and lunch for everyone. “Just because we’re a big box store, it doesn’t mean that we’re not here in Warsaw,” said store manager Jonathan Pechscott. The beds aren’t just a reward for the children too. “For us to deliver the bed, we are just as excited and happy about delivering that bed as they are getting it,” said Suellen Denney, co-president of the Fulton County SHP chapter. The Fulton County chapter recently started, but they already delivered over 100 beds since last December. Volunteers attend for a reason This year’s bed-building event held a special meaning for one Warsaw father-son duo: Perry and Dane Kaleohano. “We wanted to show our support to the community on behalf of my wife who passed away three years ago today,” said Perry. They want to continue honoring her while also serving the community through faith and generosity. “You never know what your neighbor might be going through or your friend that you haven’t talked to in a while,” said Dane. “Just try to help out the people that are in need and reach out.” You can find more information on the application and Sleep in Heavenly Peace’s mission here . https://telex.hu/sport/2026/11/08/oroszo.text: Feszültség alakult ki a jégkorong világában, miután a nemzetközi Sportdöntőbíróság (CAS) jogellenesnek ítélte az orosz sportolók eltiltását, és elrendelte Oroszország visszaengedését a tornákra. A Nemzetközi Jégkorong Szövetség (IIHF) jelezte, hogy nem ért egyet vele, de kénytelen végrehajtani a döntést, így a december végi junior-világbajnokságon az oroszok be is kerültek Norvégia helyére, a skandináv csapat pedig a másodosztályba szorult vissza – írja a Reuters és az MTI. A nemzetközi szövetség döntésének súlyos következményei lehetnek, a témáról ebben a cikkben írtunk bővebben . A CAS döntése nagy felháborodást váltott ki Európában. Svédország, Finnország, Csehország, Norvégia, Dánia, Ausztria, Lettország, Ukrajna és junior szinten Svájc jelezte, hogy nem állna ki az orosz válogatott ellen. A német szövetség elnöke pedig még a 2027 májusi férfi elit-világbajnokság rendezési jogáról is lemondana a helyzet miatt. Ennek tetejében több szponzor is jelezte, hogy orosz részvétel esetén visszavonják a vb-re szánt anyagi támogatásukat, ami komoly gondot okozhat a Nemzetközi Jégkorong Szövetségnek. Mark Carney kanadai miniszterelnök bejelentette, hogy az orosz játékosok semmiképpen sem lesznek ott az edmontoni és Red Deer-i junior vb-n. Kanada közölte azt is, hogy a hatóságok megakadályozzák, hogy az orosz sportolók és tisztviselők beutazzanak az országba. Olli Rauste, a CAS korábbi jogásza a helyzetről azt mondta, ha az IIHF nem hajtja végre a bíróság kötelező döntését az olimpiai kvalifikációhoz kapcsolódó tornákon, az a sportág olimpiai státuszát is veszélybe sodorhatja. Emellett a vízumokat megtagadó országok – például Kanada vagy Finnország – szintén kockáztatják, hogy elveszítik a jövőbeli nemzetközi sportesemények rendezési jogait. Mindennek azért is nagy a jelentősége, mert ha az IIHF-hez hasonlóan döntenek majd a többi világbajnokságról is, akkor például a felnőtt tornáról az elitbe több mint húsz év után visszakerült Ukrajna is kikerülhetne.
